items.response:
Got it: no replacement for the 2019 CX-5 in 2026, the money goes to the kitchen renovation, and an EV gets another look in 2028. I'll get you off the dealer's trade-in and promo emails and leave service and insurance mail alone.
Action: unsubscribe you from the Mazda dealer's marketing lists, filter their trade-in offers, and tell you exactly what I removed.

I don't have your green bin day saved, and holiday weeks shift collection, so I won't guess.
Action: check the city collection schedule for your address and tell you this week's green bin day.

That does sound exhausting, especially with the one morning you protect getting taken first and the in-person ask landing on a Friday. I'll plan Thu the 8th as a same-day Montreal round trip, out in the morning and home for dinner. Separately, Nate's invoice (NR-2026-118, $3,200, due Fri 25 Sep) is still waiting on which account to pay from.
Action: search trains and flights from home to Montreal for Thu the 8th (morning out, evening back), show you the best two or three with arrival times against the bank meeting, and hold off booking until you pick.

I don't have a record of what you're studying with Carlos or which things you keep getting wrong, so I'd rather not guess. What's the subject, and what tripped you up last time?
Action: search your notes and past chats for anything from your classes with Carlos, and as soon as you tell me the topic I'll write the 8 to 10 question warm-up with an answer key.

Morning! March really is a liar, snow again is rude. A hot drink and a slow start are fully justified.
Action: check today's calendar and the forecast and tell you if the snow changes anything.

A 40 minute bag wait plus a forgotten swim shirt and stuffie is a rough combination. I don't have your packing preferences saved, so I won't guess how you want it done.
Action: ask you for the rule (what you carry on, who packs what, how far ahead) and the day you fly home, save it as your standing packing rule, and build Leo's checklist for the trip home with the swim shirt and his stuffie at the top.

Pastel de nata comes from Lisbon, Portugal, specifically the Belém neighbourhood. Monks at the Jerónimos Monastery are said to have made them in the early 1800s, and a bakery nearby has been selling them since 1837. For Leo: monks invented a custard tart, and now it's Portugal's favourite treat.
Action: if he wants to taste one, find a bakery near you that makes them and send you the options.

That deserves to be said out loud: leading Instant Payouts at Lumen Pay end to end as a senior PM, and it worked. Congratulations, that's a real milestone.
Action: add the May 2026 launch to your notes as a win to pull from at review time, unless you'd rather I didn't.

The offsite is Thu 12 Nov, so I'll count business days from tomorrow to then, skipping any holidays in the stretch. I'll also mark where Tom's earlier deadlines fall inside that runway.
Action: calculate the business days from tomorrow through Thu 12 Nov and give you the number, with Tom's Q1 page deadline (6 Nov) marked as a checkpoint.

I don't have a confirmed Instant Payouts GA date saved, so I won't put one in the note. I'll draft it in your style: no em dashes, 'merchant' wording, short paragraphs of three sentences or fewer.
Action: check the roadmap and the Linear GA milestone for the date, fill it into a short draft to Olivia, and show it to you before anything is sent.

Yes, it used to be January. The season and playoffs kept getting longer, and the 2002 game was pushed into February after 9/11 and it mostly stayed there. Sunday is simply the NFL's biggest TV day.
Action: none needed, unless you want me to dig up the exact history.

Happy to, but I'd rather pull it than guess.
Action: read the family and work calendars for next week, then give you a day-by-day rundown with any conflicts and anything that needs a decision from you.

Posting the Slack draft now. I don't have Tom's favourite whisky anywhere I can see, so I won't guess a bottle.
Action: post the API error code question to #payouts-launch, then search your notes and messages for any mention of Tom's whisky and come back with what I find, or suggest a safe alternative.

Yes to pancakes at Hannah's on Sunday at 9, and I'll check the Okafor-Malhotra family calendar for conflicts before adding it.
Action: text Hannah a yes, check Sunday morning on the family calendar, and add 'Pancakes at Hannah's' at 9:00 if it's clear (otherwise tell you what clashes first).

Noted: the mid-year performance self-review in Lattice is due 2026-07-10, and I'll keep it on your radar so it doesn't sneak up. Enjoy the read tonight.
Action: set a reminder next week to start the self-review and a second one the week it's due.

Happy to. The usual shape is warm and brief, and clear that two brief changes after approval put the redo outside the original scope. I don't have the client's name, the hours involved or the contract terms, so I'll leave those as placeholders.
Action: draft the email for Priya with placeholders for the client name and hours, offering a change order and a short call, and show it to you before it goes to her.

I'll book a 30 minute walkthrough with Diego and Aisha on the 13th in the afternoon (my usual default is 25, but you said half an hour). The invite will carry an agenda: 1) walk through the new onboarding flows, 2) feedback and open questions, 3) next steps.
Action: find a 30 minute afternoon slot on the 13th that works for Diego, Aisha and you, then send the invite with that agenda.

Done, short version.
Action: add a weekly recurring event, Tuesdays 5:30 pm, Leo's swim lessons at Pam McConnell Aquatic Centre in Regent Park, starting tomorrow, on the family calendar.

Ha, a very fair question: big cake, tiny arms for blowing out candles. Sounds like a long day, so go sit down.
Action: nothing pending from me tonight; tell me if you want anything handled before bed.

That sounds like a long stretch, and I'm happy to just listen as well. On the floor: skip the broom, which pushes grit around and can scratch. Go over it with a soft brush vacuum head (beater bar off) or a dry microfibre mop first, then a barely damp microfibre pad, because wet mopping turns drywall dust into paste.
Action: stay here for the talk, and if you'd like I can add a floor cleaning list to your notes or order microfibre pads.

Merry belated Christmas! Pyjamas at 11, a third Lego truck build, and Sam and Biscuit asleep on the couch is peak Boxing Day. Enjoy every minute.
Action: nothing needed from me right now; I'll stay quiet unless you want something.

Both are on the list: memo comments to Tom by Friday, and Leo's library books from the Pape branch on Saturday morning. Heads up that Saturday morning has Leo's soccer, 9:00 to 10:00 at Jimmie Simpson Park (arrive 8:45), if the season is still running, so the library trip fits best after the game.
Action: set a Friday reminder for the memo comments and a Saturday reminder for the library pickup, after checking Pape/Danforth's Saturday hours.

I don't have a note on what Leo is obsessing over lately, and I don't have his food restrictions in front of me. The only thing I can see recently is the cushion fort, and I won't guess on food since that matters for safety. I'd check before telling Grace anything.
Action: search your notes and messages for Leo's current interests and any food allergies or restrictions, then give you a short list to pass to Grace.

Five nut-free lunches: pasta salad with chicken and cucumber, turkey and cheese pinwheels, mini pita pizzas, a rice and veggie bento with fruit, and quesadilla strips with a fruit cup. I'll keep every one completely nut free, no exceptions, and flag that packaged items need a nut-free label even if the camp is nut-aware. I don't have what you asked me about Biscuit and the ambulance, so I won't guess.
Action: search your past chats and notes for the Biscuit and ambulance question and tell you what I find, and tell me Leo's favourites if you want the lunch list tuned.

My notes show two out-of-office drafts: a January one that was saved but never switched on, and a May one (out Fri 22 May, back Mon 25 May, Aisha covering payouts) that was drafted but not confirmed on. I'll check which auto-reply is actually active and end it tomorrow morning. The new message will say you're back but catching up.
Action: check the live auto-reply in Gmail, set it to end tomorrow morning, rewrite the message to say you're back and catching up, and show it to you before saving.

Setting up a 25 minute onboarding design review with Aisha and Diego on Thu 26 Nov at 10:00. The agenda goes in the invite: KYC retry screens, empty states, open questions.
Action: check your, Aisha's and Diego's calendars for 10:00 to 10:25 that day, send the invite with the agenda, and flag any conflict before sending.

On it. I'll put a short summary in a note for Tanvi: the 2.1% guideline for 2026, anything above needs LTB approval, 90 days written notice on an N1 once every 12 months, and she can pay just the guideline amount if no LTB application exists. I'll also note that she should confirm the unit was first occupied after the cutoff, since you weren't sure about the build year.
Action: write the note with links to the official Ontario guideline and Landlord and Tenant Board pages, and give it to you to forward.

You're welcome. Tom's request for the beta merchant numbers link is still open; you said you'd deal with it after dinner.
Action: nudge you after dinner about Tom's message, and look for the link in your email if you want me to.

Welcome to Vancouver! I'll look for the earlier flight search and compare it against what you booked (Air Canada ref QX7L2P, three passengers, $1,947.66 CAD), and I'll find the Lafourcade song piece for Mei. I don't have either one in front of me, so I won't quote numbers or lyrics from memory.
Action: find the pre-booking flight search in our earlier chats and email, show Kabir the difference against $1,947.66, and pull up the Lafourcade piece for you to approve before it goes to Mei.

Here's a cleaner version: 'If a payout fails because of a bank-side error, the system shall automatically retry it without any action from the merchant.' It keeps the requirement and drops the stacked clauses.
Action: paste it into the PRD in place of the original once you say so, and I can tighten the neighbouring requirements the same way.

I don't have the contractor comparison in front of me, so I won't guess at the reasons. They should be in the reno notes or the quotes.
Action: search your notes, email and Drive for the contractor comparison and the quotes, then give you a short summary of why Nate won, ready to send to Sam.

On it. I'll group the open payouts tickets under the workstreams I have: reconciliation CSV export v2, payout status webhooks and the instant payout fee experiment. The known risks to weigh are the bank partner API migration in November and a team of roughly 2.5 engineers.
Action: pull every open payouts ticket from Linear, group by workstream, and give you a list of what looks at risk for the December launch with the reasons.

It depends on how often you actually shop and what you spend, and I don't want to guess either. The membership is worth keeping only if the savings and any rewards beat the fee.
Action: pull the last 12 months of Costco receipts and statements, count trips and total spend, compare that against the membership cost and any reward, and recommend renew, downgrade or cancel.

Setting up a 25 minute call with Olivia and Aisha on the 9th at 3:30 pm, with your three agenda items in the invite: 1) where certification stands, 2) what sales can and can't say, 3) next checkpoint.
Action: check all three calendars for 3:30 to 3:55 on the 9th, send the invite with that agenda, and flag any conflict before sending.

Surprise coming: a family style spread for three from Pai on Duncan, delivered at 6:00, with the total including delivery, tax and tip kept under $100. I'll skip anything spicy for the kid and check for any dietary restrictions before I order.
Action: pull Pai's menu, build the order, and show you the cart and the total for a quick yes before I place it.

Have a great dinner, and enjoy the pool excitement. Reminder for tomorrow: the Kitsilano pool opens at 7:00 but the lanes are closed until 9:00. Leo's checklist for the flight home is already shared with Sam.
Action: nothing needed tonight; I'll check back in the morning if you want the pool plan.

Let me check rather than guess.
Action: look up last night's Raptors final score and send you the score in one line to pass to Sam.

Sorry, that's annoying, especially with no note. I don't have your policy number or insurer details in front of me, so I'll find them before starting anything. Photos of the damage and any camera footage from the Loblaws lot will help, and it's worth checking whether the repair would come in under your deductible before you claim.
Action: search your email and Drive for the auto policy, open the claim form, and ask you to send photos of the scratch, dent and where it was parked so I can fill in the details for you to approve.

Ha, coat at your desk is a classic. Facilities always overcorrects in May.
Action: none needed, but I can send a facilities request about the AC if you want.

Wen Li needs requests through #data-requests with at least three business days of notice and a written metric definition, and Wed is close, so this should go in today. I'll draft the request with a proposed definition for you to confirm: failed payouts in the last 30 days, broken down by receiving bank.
Action: draft the #data-requests post to Wen with the metric definition and the Wednesday roadmap prep deadline, and show it to you before posting.

I'll scan your beta materials for any links to the old pricing page. If you can give me the old URL I can search exactly; otherwise I'll look for pricing links and test where each one lands.
Action: scan the beta docs in Drive and Notion for pricing links, check which are broken or redirect, and give you a list of the docs and links to fix.

I'll block Sunday 8:30 to 10:00 pm for the spy series with Sam. For your mom, anything I pick has to be sugar-free because of her type 2 diabetes, and it needs to deliver to Bandra.
Action: add the Sunday evening block to the calendar, then find two or three well-reviewed Mumbai shops with sugar-free mithai that deliver to Bandra and send you options with prices and delivery times to approve before I order.

No: in Ontario a landlord can't take a damage deposit, only a last month's rent deposit, and they can't just deduct for damage. If it's more than normal wear and tear, the landlord has to apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board, and scuffed walls usually count as normal wear. Diego can ask for the money back in writing, and apply to the LTB if they refuse. I'm not a lawyer, so he may want to check with a tenant legal clinic.
Action: put together a short note with the key points and links to the LTB and CLEO pages for you to forward to Diego.

Happy to help tidy those. I'll look at this month's notes and suggest what to keep, merge or drop, and I won't delete anything without your say.
Action: pull your personal notes created or edited this month, list them with titles and last edited dates, group them into keep, merge and probably delete, and show you the list.

A Drumheller dinosaur trip over March break sounds great. I'll find a hotel for 3 nights that week and price Tyrrell tickets for Leo by his age bracket. Drumheller is outside Calgary, so you'd likely fly into Calgary and rent a car, and I can price that once you pick the hotel.
Action: search family friendly Drumheller hotels for 3 nights in the week of the 16th and send you a few options with prices, plus the Tyrrell child ticket price.
